coronary artery dissections after blunt chest trauma can be treated with percutaneous intervention but in case of proximal dissections with subsequent intraluminal clot formation and total occlusion of coronary arteries, urgent CABG is preferred as the initial reperfusion strategy.
the proximal L-AD dissection and subsequent thrombus formation after blunt chest trauma should be treated with CABG.

coronary artery dissection after blunt chest trauma should be considered as a possible etiology for acute myocardial infraction and CABG should the preferred procedure for proximal LAD lesions with subsequent thrombus and total occlusion of LMCA.

the management of acute myocardial ischaemia after blunt chest trauma is a challenge for clinicians and the treatment strategy should be individualized according to the anatomic characteristics of each patient and the clinical presentation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of coronary artery dissection after blunt chest trauma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients with acute coronary syndrome and the treatment should be tailored to the individual patient.
